messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 Pager: p99 streaming tail latency exceeded in eu-west-2. Alert group: streaming-tail-latency. Affected service: inference-runtime. Current p99 ~ 28s, p95 ~ 1.4s, error rate for streaming connections up 12%.
jordan (sre): ack'ing. I'm on it. starting triage — checking metrics and recent deploys.
lee (neteng): looking at VPC egress metrics, I'm already seeing packet retransmit spikes between az-a and az-c, plus NAT active ports nearing pool limit in eu-west-2-nat-1.
sara (pm): customer impact: top three customers show degraded streaming sessions; one customer (AcmePlatform) reports ~40% stalled streams for the last 12 minutes. They're escalating.
jordan (sre): ok, can we confirm if this is a routing change or NAT exhaustion? no recent runtime deploys in past hour.
lee (neteng): running a quick check — trunking BGP and control-plane look stable. From our egress NAT host logs: conntrack table size at 95%, ephemeral port allocation spike. Suspect socket starvation leading to stalls and TLS handshake timeouts.
lee (neteng): paste of netstat summary:
```
# netstat -s | grep retrans
TCP:  123456 retransmits
# conntrack -S | grep entries
entries  : 948761
```
lee (neteng): also seeing elevated TLS handshake timeouts with retransmits on the 10.0.x.x -> internet path. Traceroute shows an extra hop/latency entering the provider edge from az-c.
jordan (sre): good catch. mitigation options: 1) enlarge conntrack / ephemeral port pool on NAT instances, 2) steer streaming egress away from az-c (traffic-shift), 3) spin up additional NAT nodes and update auto-scaling, 4) fallback to lower-throughput model variant for impacted tenant routes.
maya (oncall): i'm taking the next shift — joining now. jordan handing off. handing to maya.
jordan (sre): handoff: state — p99 at 28s, packet retransmits high, conntrack at 95%, customer-reported stalls. No code deploys. Lee and I are coordinating an egress steering plan.
maya (oncall): noted. I'll apply quick mitigations while we investigate root cause. priority: reduce customer impact (steer traffic + add NAT capacity).
lee (neteng): starting egress steer: updating route tables for streaming-elb to prefer az-b and az-a pools. Command i'll run:
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abcd1234 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --network-interface-id eni-azb-xxxx
```
lee (neteng): also triggering NAT pool scale on eu-west-2-nat-auto-scaling-group (+2).
devops-bot: ✅ ASG scaling triggered: eu-west-2-nat-asg increment=2. Instances launching (ami-ami-xxx).
maya (oncall): applying conntrack tuning as a short-term fix on running NAT instances: echo 262144 > /proc/sys/net/nf_conntrack_max and tune ephemeral port range. Pushing via runbook executor.
lee (neteng): after steering start: initial telemetry — retransmits down ~40% on az-c->internet links, overall p99 dropped to ~12s. still above SLO.
sara (pm): can we message impacted customers with ETA? ask ops to draft a short blurb: we're mitigating, rolling traffic, ETA 15-30m.
jordan (sre): draft blurb: "We're experiencing elevated streaming latency in eu-west-2 impacting some streaming sessions. We're actively rerouting traffic and increasing egress capacity; mitigation in progress. We'll update in 15 minutes."
maya (oncall): running tcpdump on NAT host for a short sample to verify retransmit patterns and potential asymmetric routing — saving to /tmp/nat-sample.pcap.
lee (neteng): quick tcpdump summary (SYN/ACK retrans patterns):
```
12:01:23.123456 IP a.b.c.d.443 > 10.0.1.5.54321: Flags [S.], seq 1, ack 1, win 64240
12:01:24.234567 IP a.b.c.d.443 > 10.0.1.5.54321: Flags [S.], retransmission
```
lee (neteng): also noticed DNS timeouts for some hosts from az-c resolvers; could be overloaded resolver endpoints coinciding.
maya (oncall): current status update: conntrack increased, ASG scale in progress, traffic steering applied. visible p99 improved to ~8.7s, p95 ~1.1s. streaming stalls decreased but not resolved.
jordan (sre): good. next steps: maintain steering for 30m, monitor for reversion anomalies, capture full pcap if we see additional retransmit surges, and open a ticket to audit NAT configuration and conntrack tuning historically.
sara (pm): please collect a clear customer impact summary and ETA to resolution. we need to inform sales/support.
lee (neteng): I'll keep digging provider edge metrics for signs of peering queuing or rate-limiting; will also ask cloud provider for any noisy neighbor reports on that POP.
maya (oncall): if p99 doesn't drop below 2s after full scaling and 30m steering, we'll rotate to a regional fallback plan (route eu-west-2 streaming to eu-west-1) — that's a heavier migration but available.
jordan (sre): note for postmortem: probable chain = NAT ephemeral depletion + intermittent DNS resolver delays + asymmetric path causing retransmits -> socket starvation -> streaming tail stalls.
devops-bot: 📌 Runbook step completed: conntrack_max increased, ephemeral port range applied to NAT fleet. ASG scale completed (2 new instances healthy).
maya (oncall): final check: p99 at 2.1s, p95 0.9s, error rate back down to baseline within most tenants. AcmePlatform reports sessions mostly restored. marking incident as mitigated, continuing to monitor for 1h.
lee (neteng): filing follow-up action: ticket NET-3483 — investigate provider edge latency and move to long-term fix (permanent NAT scaling + resolver redundancy).
jordan (sre): thanks team. i'll own the postmortem and include timelines, metrics, and the customer impact blurb. hand back to oncall rotation after monitoring window.
sara (pm): appreciate the rapid response. I'll prepare the customer-facing update with the current status and resend to account team.
maya (oncall): handing back to rotation in 30m. if anything regresses ping @oncall. :thumbsup:
